Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is fine on a US flight, as long as it goes in your carry-on and not your checked bag.

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limit for spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks is 100 Wh per battery. To convert, multiply mAh by the voltage (usually 3.7 V) and divide by 1,000. That puts 20,000 mAh at about 74 Wh, well under the limit. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries); [Dealectric's conversion table](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying))
- Power banks are carry-on only and are prohibited in checked baggage. If a carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- Protect the terminals from short circuits. You can leave it in its retail packaging, tape the terminals, or use a pouch or case. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))

**Check your airline's rules**
The FAA says airlines may set stricter limits on the number of power banks and on in-flight use. According to Dealectric's October 2026 roundup (a retailer's page, so verify with your airline), current policies include:
- **Southwest:** one power bank per customer, and you can't charge it from seat power.
- **American and Delta:** two per passenger, and no recharging the bank from seat outlets.
- **JetBlue:** two per customer.
- **United:** two batteries.

Several international carriers, such as Emirates and Korean Air, restrict or ban using a power bank on board. If you're flying internationally, check that airline's page before you go. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying))

**Other things to check**
- The Wh rating is usually printed on the bank, and some airlines want to see it.
- Don't fly with a damaged, swollen, or recalled power bank. ([FAA: PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))

I can suggest specific 20,000 mAh models if you're shopping for one.
